intro: Wet room installations in Borthwick Mains present a genuinely exciting opportunity to transform your bathroom — but they also demand careful planning, particularly given the character of properties in this part of Midlothian. Whether you're in a centuries-old stone cottage or a newer build on a modern estate, converting a standard bathroom into a fully waterproofed, level-access wet room is a significant investment that pays dividends in both daily comfort and long-term property value. Done properly, a wet room is one of the most practical and stylish upgrades a Borthwick Mains homeowner can make — but the local building stock means preparation and expertise really matter here.
localContext: Borthwick Mains sits in a part of Midlothian where the housing mix is genuinely varied. Older stone-built properties and period cottages dominate much of the area, and these come with their own challenges when it comes to wet room installation. Stone walls can be irregular, floors may not be level, and the underlying structure often needs more preparation before any waterproofing membrane can be applied confidently. Moisture management is critical in older homes — without proper tanking and drainage design, you risk damp working its way into original stonework and causing far more damage than you'd expect. On the modern estates in and around Borthwick Mains, the challenges are different but still present — cavity walls and timber floor joists need careful assessment before you commit to a full wet room layout. It's also worth noting that Borthwick Mains sits in a moderately hard water area, which means limescale can build up on shower fixtures, glass screens, and drainage channels over time. Specifying the right fittings and perhaps installing a scale-reducing shower head from the outset will save you maintenance headaches down the line.
serviceDetail: A professionally installed wet room in Borthwick Mains involves far more than pulling out an old bath and laying some tiles. The process typically begins with a site survey, where a qualified installer will assess your floor structure, existing drainage, wall composition, and the fall required to direct water effectively toward the drain. In stone-built Borthwick Mains properties especially, this survey stage is not something to rush. Once the design is agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped back entirely. The floor and walls are then prepared and a tanking system is applied — this is the critical waterproofing layer that protects the structure behind your tiles from water ingress. A linear or central drain is installed, and the floor is built up with a gradient — usually around 1.5% — to ensure water flows freely without pooling. Wall and floor tiles are then laid, with grout and sealant applied carefully to every joint. The final stage covers fitting your chosen shower valve, screen or fixed glass panel if required, lighting, and any additional accessories. In older Borthwick Mains properties with solid floors, the drainage route sometimes needs creative thinking to connect to existing waste pipes — your installer should walk you through this clearly before any work begins. The whole project typically takes between five and ten working days depending on the complexity of the space.
pricing: In Borthwick Mains, a professionally installed wet room typically costs between £6,500 and £12,000, with most standard conversions landing somewhere in the £7,500 to £9,500 range. Older stone-built properties and period cottages tend to sit toward the higher end of that scale because of additional preparation work — levelling floors, extra tanking layers, and sometimes rerouting drainage through thick walls. Modern estate homes are usually more straightforward and can come in closer to the lower end. The quality of tiles, choice of shower valve, and whether you're adding underfloor heating will all affect the final figure. Always get a detailed written quote that separates labour from materials.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwick Mains and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely makes a difference for a job like this. Local installers will have worked in similar stone cottages and period properties before — they'll know to check for damp courses that weren't built to handle wet room-level moisture, and they'll have trusted local contacts for materials sourcing and building control sign-off. Response times matter too. If a query comes up mid-project or a small issue needs addressing after completion, having someone nearby in Borthwick Mains or just across Midlothian means you're not waiting days for a call back.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Borthwick Mains?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more preparation than a modern home. Stone walls and uneven floors need careful assessment and often additional tanking to ensure the waterproofing layer is fully effective. An experienced installer familiar with Borthwick Mains period properties will know what to look for and how to address it before tiling begins.

faqs.q: Will the moderately hard water in Borthwick Mains cause problems in a wet room?
faqs.a: It can cause limescale to build up on glass screens, chrome fittings, and drainage channels over time. Specifying scale-resistant coatings on glass and using a quality shower head with limescale-resistant nozzles helps considerably. Regular cleaning with a mild descaler will keep everything looking good, and some homeowners also fit an inline scale reducer to the shower supply.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in a Borthwick Mains home?
faqs.a: Most wet room conversions in Borthwick Mains take between five and ten working days. Older stone properties or complex layouts can take a day or two longer due to additional preparation work on floors and walls. Your installer should give you a realistic programme before work starts so you can plan for being without that bathroom temporarily.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a Borthwick Mains property?
faqs.a: A well-designed, professionally installed wet room is generally viewed positively by buyers, particularly in the premium end of the market where Borthwick Mains properties often sit. Level-access showering is increasingly sought after for accessibility reasons too. The key is quality — a poorly installed wet room with inadequate waterproofing can put buyers off, so always use a qualified, experienced installer.
